name: app-header
title: App header
purpose: The top bar of an app: the product name or the current view's title, with an optional back link, actions and a tray for approvals that are waiting.
whenToUse: Once per screen, as the first thing in the page.
With the product name on a top-level screen, and with a back link and the view's title on a screen below one.
With the tray when something, such as an approval, must stay in sight on every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a view's title with its description and main action inside the page. Use a page header.
For moving between the main destinations on a phone. Use a tab bar.
For a message about the state of the app, such as a lost connection. Use a banner under the header.
For the main action of a view. Put a primary button in the view, never in the header.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Scrolls away with the page. Use it when the screen is short or the header holds nothing the reader needs while scrolling.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Stays at the top while the page scrolls. Use it when the back link, the actions or the tray must stay in reach.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: One row with controls of default size, 48px tall by default and 52px on a coarse pointer, at every width. The tray adds a row below it only while it holds something.

accessibility: Use a header element. Outside main it is the page's banner landmark, so a page has one.
The product name is a link to the first screen. It is not a heading.

A view has one h1. When the view has a page header, the page header's title is the h1 and the app header shows the product name. Only a view with no page header, such as a detail screen with a back link, puts its title in ds-app-header__title as the h1. Never write the title as an h1 in both.
The tray, ds-app-header__tray, is where the pending tray goes: put the pending tray's div inside it, on every signed-in screen.
The back link names where it goes: visible text such as Tasks, or aria-label="Back to tasks" when it is only the icon.
An icon-only action has an aria-label that says what it does and to what, such as Search tasks. Its icon carries aria-hidden="true".
Use a link for an action that goes to another view and a button for one that acts on this view.
Tab moves through the name or back link, then the actions, then the tray, in the order they are written. Enter follows a link, and Enter or Space presses a button.
A long title is cut with an ellipsis. Keep the full title in the document title or in the page, where it can be read whole.
An empty tray takes no space and is not announced. Leave the element in place and fill it when something is waiting.
With the sticky variant, give the scrolling container scroll-padding-top of the header's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.
